chapters.title: Find your home row
chapters.description: Start with the anchor keys and add one comfortable reach at a time.

chapters.title: Reach the upper row
chapters.description: Keep your hands anchored while you learn the upper letter keys.

chapters.title: Connect the alphabet
chapters.description: Add the lower row, then turn individual reaches into flowing words.

chapters.title: Capitals and numbers
chapters.description: Practice deliberate Shift use and dependable number entry.

chapters.title: Write complete thoughts
chapters.description: Build accuracy with punctuation and ordinary sentences.

chapters.title: Build a steady pace
chapters.description: Thirty-second accuracy checks from 15 to 80 WPM. This path is available from the start.

lessons.guidance: Rest your index fingers on F and J. Feel the raised marks, keep your wrists comfortable, and return to these anchors.

kd dk kj df jk fd kdk dkd jkd fdk kkf ddj kd dk jf fj

lessons.guidance: Use your middle fingers for D and K. Keep F and J as reference points; aim for accurate, relaxed presses.

lessons.title: A and semicolon

lessons.title: G and H inward reach

variants.text: fg jh gf hj gh hg gag hah glad hall half flag dash glass
hf gj fh jg hg gh had has glad flask; half a glass; glad
gag hah gh hg flag half glad dash; a lad has a glass flask

lessons.guidance: Reach G with the left index finger and H with the right index finger. Return to F and J after each reach.

lessons.title: Home-row word flow

variants.text: a glad lad has a flask; a half glass; a lass has a flag; glad
a lad has a glass; a glad lass has a flask; half a flag; glad
glad lads dash; a lass has a glass flask; a lad has half; glad

lessons.guidance: Use all home-row keys in short groups and words. Take your time; this lesson has an accuracy goal rather than a speed goal.

lessons.title: R and U reaches

variants.text: fr ju rf uj fur rush rural; a lad has a fur rug; hush; glad
ur ru fur rug; a glad lad rush; a rural hall has a glass jar
frf juj rfr uju; rush a fur rug; a lad has a rural glass jar

lessons.guidance: Reach R with the left index finger and U with the right index finger, returning to your home position.

lessons.title: E and I reaches

variants.text: de ki ed ik; a red fire; a dear rider; a fresh idea; ride free
rise like fire; a fair rider reads; a dear lass rides; safe rides
ed ik de ki; fresh ideas are like fire; a fair lad reads free

lessons.guidance: Use the middle fingers for E and I. Let accuracy settle before adding pace.

lessons.title: W and O reaches

variants.text: sw lo ws ol; slow flow; a wide road; a rider follows a red owl
a slow row of red roses; a wise lad follows a wide road; flow
ow wo sw lo; words flow like a slow ride; a wise rider reads

lessons.guidance: Use your ring fingers for W and O. Keep the movement small and return to the home row.

lessons.title: Q and P reaches

variants.text: aq ;p qa p; quip pupil; a pure pupil reads; a proper purple jar
a pale quail; a pupil reads proper words; a purple owl; equip
qa p; aq ;p; a pupil equips a proper ship; pure words; purple

lessons.guidance: Use the little fingers for Q and P. Short pauses between groups are fine in these foundation lessons.

lessons.title: T and Y inward reach

variants.text: ft jy tf yj; try the little story; the quiet pupil types steadily
a quiet day at the shop; the pupil types a short story; stay steady
ty yt ft jy; the happy pupil types; try a little story at the desk

lessons.guidance: Use the index fingers for T and Y. Keep your shoulders relaxed as you return to the anchor keys.

lessons.title: Upper-row word flow

variants.text: the quiet pupil types a little story at the desk; a steady day
a happy writer reads the paper; the words flow at a steady rate
the ship sails past the shore; a quiet pupil writes a short story

lessons.guidance: Connect the upper and home rows. Read a short group ahead without rushing the current word.

lessons.title: V and M letter reaches

variants.text: fv jm vf mj; move the silver mug; a small river flows past home
a mild idea moves slowly; the silver vase is at home; very steady
vm mv fv jm; a small mouse moves past the vase; improve every day

lessons.guidance: Reach V and M with the index fingers. Keep each hand near its home position rather than moving the whole wrist.

lessons.title: C and N letter reaches

variants.text: calm hands can learn; a clear mind notices each new reach and return
new letters connect into words; practice each reach with care and calm
cn nc; a nice river scene; calm practice can create a clear new rhythm

lessons.guidance: Add C and N to your letter practice. Use the left middle finger for C and the right index finger for N.

lessons.title: X and B letter reaches

variants.text: a blue box sits by the desk; relax the hands and build a calm rhythm
bring the box back; careful practice builds flexible hands and clear words
xb bx; a brave fox explores a blue box; balance every reach with rest

lessons.guidance: Use the left ring finger for X and the left index finger for B. Move deliberately, then return to the home row.

lessons.title: Z completes the alphabet

variants.text: a zebra rests near the quiet river; zero rushed keys and a relaxed pace
the lazy fox examines a bright quartz box; every new letter has a place
z zz zone zero; a quiet breeze moves past the cozy brick house at dawn

lessons.guidance: Use the left little finger for Z. The full English alphabet is now available for practice.

lessons.title: Every letter, one rhythm

variants.text: quick brown foxes jump by a quiet garden while zebras rest near the lake
mix bright quartz pebbles with a few clay jars and pack the box gently
every calm practice session builds the next small piece of a useful skill

lessons.guidance: Practice words across all three letter rows. Finish the current word carefully before moving on.

lessons.title: Full-alphabet word check

variants.text: the quiet fox brings a small blue box to the garden while a lazy zebra rests nearby
a quick writer makes clear plans and checks every word before moving to the next line
practice gives each finger a dependable path so the whole alphabet can feel familiar

lessons.guidance: Connect complete words at a comfortable pace. A clean final passage and honest insertion accuracy both matter.

lessons.title: Capital letters on the left

variants.text: Ada asks Dave for a Fresh Draft. A Brave Gardener brings a Red Vase to the Desk.
Grace and Ava share a Warm Drink. A Clear Draft gives Dave a Better Starting Point.
Zara reads a Short Story. A Quiet Garden gives Ada a Calm Space for Fresh ideas.

lessons.guidance: Hold the opposite Shift key while typing a capital. For left-hand letters, use right Shift; avoid relying on Caps Lock.

lessons.title: Capital letters on the right

variants.text: Joy and Kim meet Luke near Oak Hill. I hope Your Morning is calm and Your Notes are clear.
Hope joins Nora for Lunch. Lily keeps Her Notes in a Paper folder beside the Yellow mug.
Milo and Julia plan a New Journey. Oliver keeps His Map near the quiet Lake.

lessons.guidance: For right-hand capital letters, use left Shift. Return to a relaxed home position after each word.

lessons.title: Names and sentence starts

variants.text: Ada and Noah visit Cedar Park on Monday. They bring a small notebook and write clear notes.
Every Friday, Maya reads a new story with Liam. A short practice can fit into a busy day.
Keep the names River House and Oak Lane clear. Good habits grow through small daily actions.

lessons.guidance: Alternate lowercase words with meaningful capital letters. Watch the exact displayed case rather than the physical keyboard.

lessons.title: Numbers 1 through 5

5 4 3 2 1 54 43 32 21 15 543 432 321; write 12 notes and check 4 small tasks.
13 24 35 41 52 12345 54321; place 2 cups by shelf 3 and keep 5 pages in folder 14.

lessons.guidance: Locate 1 through 5 deliberately. Accuracy is the goal; a browser cannot verify which finger you actually use.

lessons.title: Numbers 6 through 0

variants.text: 6 7 8 9 0 67 78 89 90 06 678 789 890; room 207 has 8 chairs and 6 clean desks.
68 79 80 96 07 67890 09876; keep 7 notes in box 40 and place 9 cards on shelf 6.

lessons.title: Numbers in useful text

variants.text: On 24 May, room 18 needs 6 tables and 32 chairs. Please label each box from 1 to 9.
Practice log 204: 15 minutes on Monday, 20 on Tuesday and 12 on Friday. Keep the notes clear.
The sample order has 3 blue pens, 8 green cards and 14 folders. Reference code: 50729.

lessons.guidance: Practice numbers as part of ordinary writing. These are training examples, not real contact or financial details.

lessons.title: Commas and full stops

variants.text: Take a breath, relax your hands, and read the next word. Clear writing begins with small accurate steps.
The room is quiet, the desk is ready, and the page is open. A short practice is enough for today.
Start slowly, notice the difficult reach, and try again. Each careful attempt adds useful evidence.

lessons.guidance: Use commas and full stops without dropping the following space. Keep the sentence rhythm comfortable.

lessons.title: Apostrophes in context

variants.text: It's a quiet morning, and Nora's notebook is open. Don't rush the words; there's time to be accurate.
We're building a steady habit. A learner's progress doesn't need to look the same every single day.
I'll check the writer's notes after lunch. You're welcome to slow down when a new pattern feels difficult.

lessons.guidance: Watch contractions and possessive apostrophes. Correct an error before you commit its word with Space.

lessons.title: Questions and emphasis

variants.text: Are your shoulders relaxed? Can you return to the home row without looking? Take your time!
Which word needs another try? What changed after a short rest? Notice the small improvements!
Ready for a clear sentence? Keep the final mark in view, finish the thought, and pause!

lessons.guidance: Use the displayed question and exclamation marks. Treat the extra reach as part of the word rather than a separate rush.

lessons.title: Colons and semicolons

variants.text: Practice plan: begin with accuracy; add speed when the movement feels dependable. Keep a short note.
Three useful habits: sit comfortably, return to the anchors, and rest often; consistency takes time.
Today's focus: careful punctuation; tomorrow's focus: a smoother return from each difficult reach.

lessons.guidance: Use Shift for the colon and the unshifted semicolon where your keyboard requires it. Follow the displayed text exactly.

lessons.title: Quotes, brackets and hyphens

variants.text: Write "steady progress" on the card, add (one small goal), and keep the label [practice] easy to read.
A well-placed pause can help. Keep the note "accuracy first" beside the page (and relax your hands).
Use the labels [ready], [practice], and [review]. The phrase "little by little" describes a long-term habit.

lessons.guidance: Read opening and closing punctuation as a pair. This course shows logical characters, not a hardware-specific key map.

lessons.title: Complete-sentence check

variants.text: On Tuesday, Maya wrote: "I'll practice for 15 minutes." Her next goal was simple: clear words, calm hands, and a steady rhythm.
Can a small routine make a difference? Noah's answer was "yes"; he kept 3 short notes (one per session) and reviewed them on Friday.
The plan has 4 steps: read, type, check, and rest. A good session isn't a race; it's a chance to build dependable movement.

lessons.guidance: Combine case, numbers and punctuation. Complete two different passages accurately before moving on.

lessons.title: Steady 15 WPM

variants.text: Begin with a calm breath and a comfortable position. Read a little ahead, press each key deliberately, and let a steady rhythm develop without chasing the timer.
A quiet practice can be useful even on a busy day. Keep your hands relaxed, finish each word carefully, and give the next movement enough attention.
The first goal is dependable movement. A small accurate passage is a good place to begin, and a short pause between sessions can help you return with a clear mind.

lessons.guidance: Hold at least 15 credited WPM for the full 30 seconds with 98% input accuracy. Corrected mistakes still count.

lessons.title: Comfortable 25 WPM

variants.text: Small improvements often come from a simple routine. Open the page, choose one useful goal, and practice with enough care to notice both the easy patterns and the difficult ones.
Each word is a short sequence of familiar movements. Keep the next letters in view while your fingers finish the current group, then continue at a comfortable pace.
A clear desk and a relaxed posture can make practice easier to begin. Work through the sentence steadily, correct the current word when needed, and keep your attention on the text.

lessons.guidance: Aim for a repeatable 25 WPM and 98% input accuracy over the full 30 seconds. Let the words stay clear.

lessons.title: Fluent 35 WPM

variants.text: Progress becomes easier to understand when the evidence is honest. Corrected mistakes remain part of input accuracy, while the final text shows how well the finished passage matches its target.
A good practice routine leaves room for both effort and rest. Notice the movement that feels awkward, return to a manageable pace, and finish the sentence with the same care you used at the start.
The goal of fluency is useful writing rather than a single impressive number. Keep a regular pace, read the punctuation clearly, and let accurate repetitions strengthen the patterns you already know.

lessons.guidance: Build a steady 35 WPM at 98% input accuracy. Use two different variants to show that the result is repeatable.

lessons.title: Confident 45 WPM

variants.text: Reliable typing connects attention, movement, and language. A familiar phrase can feel effortless, but an unusual word still deserves a careful look before the fingers commit to its sequence.

When the rhythm becomes comfortable, protect its accuracy. A rushed correction can cost more time than a deliberate first attempt, so keep reading ahead while each hand returns to a dependable position.

Measured progress is more helpful than a perfect-looking result without evidence. The timer includes idle moments, the accuracy includes corrected errors, and every completed attempt can guide the next focused practice.

lessons.guidance: Sustain 45 WPM with 98% input accuracy. Keep the whole 30-second attempt accurate instead of relying on a short burst.

lessons.title: Sustained 60 WPM

variants.text: A dependable skill should remain useful when the text changes. Work through this unfamiliar passage with a balanced rhythm, give the less common combinations enough attention, and keep the final punctuation as accurate as the first word.

Fast writing is easier to maintain when the movements are economical. Avoid unnecessary tension, allow each finger to return naturally, and use your attention to follow the meaning and structure of the sentence.

The most useful comparison is a like-for-like one. Language, keyboard layout, duration, and correction rules all affect the task, so this ladder keeps those conditions fixed while the target pace increases.

lessons.guidance: Reach 60 credited WPM at 98% input accuracy for 30 seconds. A paused or early-finished attempt remains practice only.

lessons.title: Controlled 80 WPM

variants.text: Fluency is a balance of anticipation and control. Read far enough ahead to prepare the next movement, keep unfamiliar letter combinations precise, and resist the temptation to trade reliable accuracy for a brief increase in pace.

Strong typing remains calm when the passage becomes more demanding. Maintain an even rhythm through the longer words, notice each punctuation mark, and let the full thirty-second result reflect sustained control rather than a single burst.

A well-practiced movement pattern gives attention back to the writing itself. Use that freedom to follow the sentence carefully, keep the hands comfortable, and finish this attempt with the same deliberate accuracy that began it.

lessons.guidance: Demonstrate a controlled 80 WPM and 98% input accuracy for the full 30 seconds on two distinct passages.
